2. If you are doing something like a scar similar to the look I did, I found it easier to mold the wax and adhere it first. Then, use setting powder to hold it in place. title: Non-irritating & Soothing cleanser
text:
This has brought relief. My eyelids and lashes get a thorough cleansing with no irritation or burning whatsoever.

I had cataract surgery 6 months ago and was prescribed steroid drops for 2 weeks after the procedure. Initially, I had minimal issues with irritation, dry feeling or redness. Same experience after the procedure was completed on the 2nd eye.

Approximately a month after the 2nd procedure, both eyes, but especially the right one, were no longer white (slight redness), were irritated and felt dry and scratchy. I began using the Systane eye drops that I had been given at the time of surgery but, in short order, I made an appointment with the ophthalmologist. He put me back on a reduced frequency of the steroid drops for a short time period and during the follow up(s) recommended that I continue using Systane to relieve the dry, itchy, irritating sensation.

I “did“ the Systane for a month or so but noticed my eyelids were slightly more “crusty” in the morning than I had ever experienced. Then a major redness (in both eyes) hit. It was so bad that I thought that I had pink eye.

Back to the ophthalmologist, (No, I haven’t changed shampoo or laundry detergent; Yes, I still work in a clean room, environmentally controlled lab; No, I don’t have any new workplace exposures) back on the steroid drops and still needing Systane (several times/day) to temporarily relieve the dry scratchy feeling.

Little did I know that statistically over 30% of all cataract surgery patients experience the same irritation and dryness issues that I did. Most, like my mother-in-law, simply rely on eye drops for relief - in my mother-in-laws case - 4 times per day for over 2 years since her surgery.

The relief for me has been a combination of incorporating the Bruder eye heat pad (w/hygienic eyelid sheets) and the OCuSOFT Oust Demodex cleanser. The improvement in my eye discomfort level was almost immediate. In the 2 weeks that I have used this combo I have used ZERO eye drops.

I specifically chose the OCuSOFT Oust Demodex cleanser because an ophthalmologist stated in his review that it was “tolerated” by virtually all of his patients for daily use.

Did I have Demodex mites or clogged eyelid oil glands or just getting old? I don’t know, but the Bruder heat combined with the the OCuSOFT Oust Demodex cleanser (Tulip Oil) worked for me without any discomfort. Totally Satisfied!

title: Not worth the current price
text:
I've used a number of Jack Black products over the years, but this was my first experience with the MP 10 Epic Moisture oil. I have a short (7mm) beard as well as a short haircut, and tried using the oil on both as directed. Overall I didn't find it to be bad but also didn't feel that it lived up to its price.

There are three things I liked about this oil. The packaging and bottling was very good. It comes in a well-made glass bottle with a good pump. I found the instructions to be detailed and precise. I also liked the fact that the scent was almost nonexistent. Some reviewers say it has a faint lemon/citrus smell. It reminded me more of a glass of water with some lemon wedges in it. Overall, pleasant.

What I didn't like was the texture of the oil. It was rather thin compared to other beard/hair oils I've used and seemed like it required about twice as much product. While it didn't leave a greasy feeling on my hands, or in my beard or hair, it also didn't provide much in the way of moisturizing/softening. Again, it was fine, but not "$35 per bottle fine."

I've used two other beard oils on Amazon which I felt were a particularly good value: Gibs, and The Art of Shaving. Both have stronger and more nuanced scent profiles, but both are thicker and have much better moisturizing properties. I'll continue to stick with those.

title: A Powerful Preventative Tool For A Nation Of Diabetics!
text:
I never suspected I would be writing a review about what appears to be a sander to use on ones feet but here I am doing exactly that.
About 18-20 months ago my husband who has adult onset diabetes injured his large toe. He was on a job site and accidentally tripped over something but because of advanced diabetes he has neuropathy which has caused him to lose most sensation in his feet. I discovered the injury as he was putting on his socks and when I began to put medication and a bandage on his toe, the end of the toe nearly fell off in my hand. So needless to say a long complicated process began to save his toe; possibly his entire foot.
As we age our feet do too. We may get thick calluses which can crack deep into the layers of the skin that are very painful and make the feet susceptible to infection, an infection that can easily become a long standing crisis not just for a diabetic but for everybody when their feet begin to misbehave. Yes, even you! Believe it or not we are still trying to get his feet to heal. Foot Cream of every kind in the house, epsom salt foot soaks, special socks and shoes. Bandaids come in more shapes, sizes and uses than one can imagine. Sports tape, implements to grind the callus down before they crack, and on and on until one wants to pull their hair out. Your entire life focus revolves around diabetic care! I can honestly say that until this happened I had never given a thought to diabetes and now it is all I think of or so it seems.
So at this point, I was frustrated, frightened and more than a little angry. I finally purchased a rasp and used it to sand the calluses on my husbands feet. At the same time I was having my own problems with my feet but had no idea that my feet were going thru the same thing. Ouch!
Now I was really getting worried because the rasp was just not effective enough to get this stuff under control and I didn't know what to do when a strange thing happened. I purchased a Dremel tool to help with some heavy cleaning I needed to do and as I used it, it occurred to me that something like this could be beneficial for the foot problem if it wasn't so dangerous.
That thought as most of mine do eventually deserted me but one day I was browsing Amazon for foot care and I saw what appeared to be a Dremel and initially thought my page had flipped. But I was intrigued so I decided to compare it to mine and that is when I discovered it is a foot Dremel! What? No! Really? Yep, a foot Dremel. Well I guess you know I spent hours on Amazon reviewing these things and this product had so many outstanding reviews I decided to give it a try.
What a blessed relief this little tool has become, a virtual life saver. I read the instructions because there is an appropriate way to have good foot hygiene and by this time I wanted nothing less than the best. We immediately began foot baths with a little Apple Cider Vinegar, sometimes Epsom Salts, or Hydrogen Peroxide, anything safe to help soften the calluses. Then I turned on my foot dremel and OMG! Once I practiced how to use it without causing further damage it was as if a miracle had occurred. The deep fissures in his feet are healing fast enough that more aren't developing and the tool is has a small surface so I used it on the toe that he had injured. We thought that toe had healed and were focusing on the calluses by then. Anyway a callus had developed on the toe but it looked OK. Well, there is ok and then there is OK! As the callus began to disappear I could see flecks of red so I felt bad because I thought I had been careless with the tool. The second time I used it on the toe which was red and painful by now three pin point holes began to bleed. Suddenly I began to realize that those were the place his toe nearly fell off. The infection had never healed! The wound had sealed over for all of that time just waiting, a spectre of death stalking my husband!
Within 3-4 days the redness around his toenail began to ease and the holes are still open but now they can heal from the inside out. Such relief! Such gratitude washed over me because if that infection had been allowed to brood much longer it may have flooded his entire body with infection, life threatening infection!
I know this is a long story but I wanted to share this journey to instill the importance of foot hygiene whether you have diabetes or not yet....? One does not wait until their feet are in crisis mode before beginning good self care, which includes and instrument such as this. When you think you need it, you are likely wishing you already had one.
So, good proactive foot hygiene, a foot dremel (my words) something adequate to do foot soaks and appropriate things to aid in softening the calluses before they form deep painful fissures and the will to see it thru.
The reason I chose this particular instrument is because of the great reviews. Many items receive good reviews but when you look at the number of the reviews and they are consistently good with far less negative ones it is a good indicator that the item is at least worth a try so watch the numbers. They can indicate good but if there is just a few reviews VS lots of reviews then you know you are likely safe.
I highly recommend this item for yourself, gifts for the hard to shop for person and encourage you to educate yourselves on what foot hygiene consists of and begin it as a preventative measure then encourage your loved ones too.
I have not received compensation of any kind for writing this book, other than the potential to help others avoid the agony, despair and long arduous hours of trying to stay ahead of an unexpected enemy threatening one's life.
Thank you for taking the time to read this. Well what are you waiting for-get going!

I get headaches, clogged ears, head pressure, dizziness. So I already have horrible health anxiety with that.

About two weeks ago, my left eye started feeling weird. I couldn’t explain why, my vision felt off? I also had terrible head pressure so I figured it was caused by my allergies. Then that eye dried up and the following day, my right eye followed. I freaked out. Thought every possible thing could be wrong with me. I ran to the drug store and bought expensive dry eye drops, and they didn’t help. I ended up going to the eye doctor and she couldn’t really see anything wrong with my eyes. But I knew there was! She said they were a little dry and told me to continue my drops and maybe get tested for my thyroid. I’m like uhh okay then. That gave me even MORE anxiety. She did ask me if I had any discharge or white stuff in the corner of my eye, at that point, I hadn’t yet.

I noticed the last couple weeks I also had some weird white flakes on the tip of my eyelashes and thought “weird I’ve been getting all this lint on my eyes lately” so I didn’t bring that up. The day after the eye doctor, I woke up to my left eye crusted shut a bit, and white gunk in the corner of my eyes. I felt like my left eye looked a little swollen and had an super light purple tint to it. Everybody said I was crazy and it wasn’t purple. 😒 I know my body and it didn’t look right to me.

My brother ended up coming over to visit and I brought up my eye issue and he’s like “maybe you have too many mites” and I’m like “Get out of here! That’s not what I have. I just have dry eyes from allergies” sure enough, I get online and start reading about people who also experienced this. So I ordered this and wow. I’ve only used it for 24hours now and so much white stuff is coming out of my eyelash follicles. I guess because their dying and that’s the waste?! My eyes feel so much better. Not sticky and weighed down. I actually had a little bit of tears last night. I haven’t been able to cry tears in almost three weeks. My eyes look refreshed and tiny white oil glands I had under my ears are basically disappearing. My eyes still feel dry but I’m hoping that gets better in time.

I would also get weird break outs and kind of like hot flashes with them. And also hives. Random hives on my face. I don’t know if that’s related but I’m thinking possibly if I’ve been allergic to their waste. I really think this started possibly because I’ve been using an oil based cleanser from a local shop. I’ve used their products religiously for over a year. I guess it wasn’t cleaning my face properly and giving them more stuff to feed from. Creepy to think about.

title: Cilantro of shave soaps
text:
Reading the reviews it's obvious that the smell of Arko is like the flavor of cilantro: some people seem to be sensitive to it and really don't like it.

I'm one if those people. The smell is really off-putting. I get a strong chemical smell, with notes of a medicine called Dimetapp that they used to give me when I was a kid.

You can mitigate the scent somewhat unwrapping the soap and letting it breathe, but it smelled up my medicine cabinet.

The shaving stick is a great way to apply and manage the soap. It makes a great lather, and gives a decent shave. Especially at this price point.

However, it dries it my skin, which I can't get past. If it didn't, I'd just store it in the garage to deal with the smell (the shell of this will definitely keep bugs and pests away).

title: Smaller than expected
text: Item is very cute and convenient for traveling but not ideal for most makeup items. It is a lot smaller in reality than it looks in the picture. title: Waste of Money
text: This is the most expensive nailpolish I've ever gotten. For the price, I expected the polish to last, go on smoothly and have good coverage. It did just the opposite. The polish is thin, doesn't cover, either the product or brush are cheap, it runs on your nails because it's so thin and it chips in less than two days. To be fair, I did not use a base coat, but for the price I expected a lot more from this product. I can't even review it for keeping my nails healthy because it didn't stay. I will NOT purchase again.

title: Didn’t work and turns yellowish-brown after a few days
text: I was really disappointed in this, been using it off and on for months and it hasn’t strengthened my nails at all. It also starts to oxidize in two days, getting yellow then brown so it makes my nails look like they’re  dirty! Sure enough when I removed it with acetone the cotton ball turned yellowish-brown and my own nail was actually clean underneath. Very odd effect. I wouldn’t mind the discoloration as much if it actually worked but my nails still tore, broke, remained thin and this polish chips off easily. It goes on smooth and seems thick at first, but it’s all downhill from there. Maybe the other formulas from this line work better? Wish I could get a refund!

title: The zipper detached the first time I used it
text: I like the fact that it was a locking makeup case. I dislike the fact the zipper doesn't stay on and without the zipper it doesn't lock.  The first time I used it the pulley thing on the zipper detached because the space was too open. I put it back on and squeezed it back shut.  It worked for a little while before the space opened up again and I had to put it back on and squeeze it shut again. The 3rd or 4th time this happened the top of the zipper completely broke off and there's no way to fix it again. Without the zipper top there's no way to lock the bag and it's completely pointless. You would think it'd be mean to where the zipper can't be pulled off especially since that's the main way you lock the bag. Not sure if anyone else has experienced this problem or if maybe I had a default bag. It's only been 2 months and I can no longer return my bag to find out if replacement one would be better.

title: Some brushes are better than others.
text: I got these brushes when they were on sale ($9 for 32 brushes...), and I didn't expect much for the price but I read some reviews and they seemed worth your money.  They came in an easily-washable bag and were organized by size, none were missing, and they were packaged well.  I didn't notice a bad chemical smell like some reviews said they had, but I still washed them like you should with any new brush.  The larger brushes, like the contour, blush, etc.  brushes were quite soft and flexible, the bristles flex and conform to your face.  But the small brushes were just very dense and hard to use.  They were very stiff and rigid.  They felt soft in your fingers but when you use them on your face, they don't flex much and they get kind of pokey.  The only use for the small eye brushes is packing, because you cant use them like a regular brush because of their stiffness.  They were just too dense, that's all.  But the larger brushes are very soft and good for blending.  They apply product evenly and smoothly.  I use them quite often.  They tend to not pick up much product, at least for me, so you have to keep dipping them into the pans often.  But I would say that the larger brushes are worth your money.
